references.text: Sisera gathered all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people who were with him—a parallel to the great army with horses and chariots in Joshua 11:4
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would become as numerous as the sand on the seashore, using the same imagery that describes the enemy's vast army
Jacob reminds God of the promise of descendants like the sand by the sea, the same expression used for the enemy's great number
The Midianites and Amalekites lay in the valley as numerous as locusts, and their camels were without number like the sand on the seashore—a similar description of an overwhelming enemy army
The Philistines gathered for war with thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and foot soldiers like the sand on the seashore—the same imagery describing a large enemy force
The Canaanites had iron chariots, showing their military strength with chariots, similar to the threat in Joshua 11:4
Solomon's army with chariots and horses shows how the Israelites later used the same military resources as their enemies
